title: Digitaal Vlaanderen's 326 public repositories evidence an open-source operating culture, not just a policy
content:
Digitaal Vlaanderen is the Flemish digital government agency: 640 staff, 326 public GitHub repositories, and publisher of the Vlaamse bouwstenen, Flanders' shared digital building blocks.

The research draws its conclusion from the repository count specifically. A published open-source policy costs nothing and is common across European public administrations, whereas 326 public repositories is the by-product of people working in the open routinely, which is much harder to manufacture. The number is used as evidence about operating culture, not as a measure of code quality or of anything else.

That matters for how the lead is approached. An agency already working in public can evaluate an openly licensed record layer on its merits without first settling a procurement argument about licence models, and as publisher of the bouwstenen it is positioned to make a component available to others rather than merely consume one. Like the other Benelux public bodies in the corpus it sits on a parallel track — institution, not supplier.
